Due to liver dysfunction 1 month after starting the treatment, the regimen was changed to moxifloxacin 400 mg/day plus clarithromycin 800 mg/day. clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old man with a history of aquarium management and an arm injury presented with chronic skin nodules and an ulcer on his right upper extremity. Initial workup included a positive T-SPOT.TB test and an excisional biopsy that was negative for M. tuberculosis by culture and PCR. A second excisional biopsy revealed non-specific histopathology (inflammatory cells, no granulomas) but subsequent cultures and PCR sequencing confirmed M. marinum. Treatment involved multiple antibiotic regimen changes due to side effects (rifabutin + clarithromycin, then moxifloxacin + clarithromycin, then linezolid + clarithromycin), leading to clinical improvement over 7 months, with the nodule flattening and post-inflammatory pigmentation fading, though scarring remained.

Histopathology from the second excisional biopsy showed moderate infiltration of inflammatory cells but no epithelioid granulomas, multinucleated giant cells, or necrosis.
Subsequent cultures from the second biopsy detected colonies on Ogawa medium, and PCR sequencing confirmed M. marinum.

Treatment involved multiple antibiotic regimen changes (rifabutin + clarithromycin, then moxifloxacin + clarithromycin, then linezolid + clarithromycin) due to side effects, leading to improvement over 7 months.
The skin nodule flattened, and post-inflammatory pigmentation faded, with scarring remaining after treatment.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Initial excisional biopsy cultures and PCR were negative for M. tuberculosis, despite a positive T-SPOT.TB test. The definitive identification of M. marinum from the second biopsy further ruled out M. tuberculosis as the causative agent for the current infection.
